findings.finding: The reported quarter screens roughly at the ~$5.6M revenue bar. In favour: Q1 FY27 medical sales were $3.95M (+388% y/y). Backlog drew down from $9.12M to $7.73M in Q1 as medical orders converted, and the 10-Q names an industrial rebound in Q2. Against: the Q2 FY26 comparison carried $2.43M of clean-energy sales, and Q1 FY27 clean energy was only $0.32M with no solar shipments. Medical has to roughly double y/y again to deliver the consensus +8-10% y/y.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Rebuilt from confirmed releases only: Q1 FY27 (2026-07-08) revenue $5.66M vs $5.60M consensus, +3.69%; Q4 FY26 (2026-05-28) record year, -8.47%; Q3 FY26 (2026-01-13) -0.48%; Q2 FY26 (2025-10-14) revenue missed per Reuters, -3.57%. One up in four, and a record year was sold.
findings.why_not_priced: The company gave no quantified Q2 figure and held no Q1 call. The market's expectation sits at consensus ~$5.6M, close to Q1's run-rate. Nothing here is a number the market lacks; this is an inside-guide reported-quarter read.
findings.independence: Q2 FY26 market split for the clean-energy comparison: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000806172/000117152025000316/ex99-1.htm . Q1 FY27 market split: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/SOTK/sono-tek-corporation-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-hm8k1tlg29dx.html . Both are company documents, and the mix they show cuts both ways.

findings.finding: Gross margin should stay elevated on medical mix. Q1 FY27 gross margin was 57% vs 52% a year earlier, 'attributed to product mix and higher-value medical device sales', against FY26's 51%. If Q2 again ships mostly medical and little clean energy, gross margin near the mid-50s supports EPS at or above the $0.04 end of the split EPS bar, even with opex rising as sales and engineering staff are added (the 10-Q says marketing and sales expense will increase in FY27).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 FY27 the margin expanded 5 points with operating income +86%, and the stock rose +3.69%. In Q4 FY26, record profitability came with -8.47%.
findings.why_not_priced: The EPS bar is split between $0.04 (Benzinga) and $0.05 (Zacks). If the market expected a mid-50s margin to persist, both sources would sit at $0.05 or above. Partly priced.
findings.independence: This shares a document with finding 1, the Q1 release and 10-Q mix. It is a separate line (margin, not revenue), but the same mix assumption drives both.

findings.finding: Backlog will print sharply higher and the release will likely cite post-quarter backlog. Q2-end backlog includes the >$3.6M medical line order of 2026-08-11 on top of the $7.73M Q1-end level. The ~$7.19M clean-energy order of 2026-09-30 (10 systems, largest aggregate order in company history) brings backlog from the two programs alone to >$10.79M. Both programs ship mainly in FY2028, which starts 2027-03-01.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 backlog rose 50% q/q to $11.21M and the stock fell -3.57% that day on a revenue miss. The order announcements moved the stock more than prints: +18.47% on 2026-09-30.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: both orders were press-released and the stock rose 18% on the second and 56% over 20 days. What remains unpriced is the total backlog figure, including ordinary bookings, and whether FY28 shipping commentary firms. A stock that had not priced the orders would sit nowhere near its 52-week high.
findings.independence: The August order release, a separate document: https://finviz.com/news/380415/sono-tek-receives-record-order-of-over-36-million-for-a-single-integrated-production-line

findings.finding: H2 FY27 guide risk. FY27 guidance is 'relatively flat to modestly higher' than $20.9M, and H1 will be roughly $11.2M if Q2 meets consensus, which implies H2 of about $9.7-10.3M, down from H2 FY26's ~$10.6M. Both record orders ship mainly in FY2028, not FY27. Northland cut its FY27 EPS estimate to $0.10 from $0.11 on 2026-09-30, the same day as the order. With Q1 $0.05 plus Q2 $0.04-0.05, that implies roughly $0.00-0.01 for all of H2. The midyear call is where management restates FY27 and could describe an H2 trough before the FY28 ramp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY27 flat-to-modest guide was given with the Q4 FY26 release on 2026-05-28, when the stock fell -8.47%. On 2025-10-14 the FY26 guide was raised to modest growth and the stock still fell -3.57% on a revenue miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the flat-to-modest guide is public and the estimate cut is in the wire. But a stock up 56% into the print, at its 52-week high, is trading the FY28 order book, not an FY27 H2 trough. If the market had priced an H2 trough, the run-up would have faded after the order day rather than extending +4.3% over the last 5 sessions. This lands inside the existing guide, so a reaffirmation is not news; the negative needs a cut or explicit H2-down language.
findings.independence: Company guide reiterated on slide 19 of the 2026-08-20 deck ('FY 2027 Revenue Projected to Be Flat to Modest Growth... Backlog and Revenue Will Be Lumpy'): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/806172/000117152026000231/ex99-1.htm

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: the stock is +56.2% over 20 days and 1.8% below its 52-week high at $7.03 (about $110M market cap). The move was driven by already-announced orders (+18.47% on 2026-09-30) and extended +4.3% in the last 5 sessions. The print brings the first conference call since May. On this name the last confirmed prints were sold three times in four, including -8.47% on a record year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Confirmed-release reactions: +3.69, -8.47, -0.48, -3.57. Median absolute move ~3.6%, one up in four.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is the price. The question is whether it is complete. With no options there is no skew to say so, and short interest is negligible (~1 day to cover), so no short cover will support the stock on a disappointment. This is a proxy, not a company number.
findings.independence: Tape figures are from the sealed baseline (run_up_20d 56.22, pct_from_52w_high -1.82). The order-day reaction, a different source: https://www.rttnews.com/story.aspx?Id=3695440

findings.finding: Insiders net-exercised expiring $3.25 options in October and kept the shares; there were no open-market sales near the high. The CFO exercised 5,488 on 2026-10-05 (2,877 withheld at $6.20, holds 23,865). The COO exercised 9,978 on 2026-10-08 (4,804 withheld at $6.75, holds 5,174). In July the CFO had sold 8,346 shares at $5.13, and two Form 144s were filed on 2026-07-21 and 2026-07-23.
findings.why_not_priced: Form 4s are public and tiny. Net exercises that keep shares the week before a print are a weak tell that insiders are not selling into the high, which is all this is.
findings.independence: COO Form 4: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/806172/000117152026000296/ownership.xml (2026-10-09). The July CFO sale is from https://www.themarketsdaily.com/2026/10/02/northland-securities-weighs-in-on-sono-tek-fy2027-earnings.html and points the other way.

baseline_tension: There is no skew. The +56% run-up near the 52-week high on announced orders cuts against any long and agrees with my mild negative lean. Negligible short interest means no squeeze offset.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): the H2 guide-risk finding lands inside the already-stated flat-to-modest FY27 guide, so it moved toward 0, from -1.0 to -0.7
'A reaction history built from the wrong events': rebuilt the base rate from the four confirmed releases (median |move| ~3.6%, 1 of 4 up); this supported p_up 45 and did not change other sizes
Rule 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 6.0 to 6.5, given 77% realised vol and a guide-bearing midyear call
Rule 7: short interest checked (negligible), so the negatives stand without a squeeze haircut
Rules 1 and 3: the reported-quarter positives were already small against a name that sells beats; left standing
